title: Thursday, September 10, 2026

headline.title: PPI came in on consensus and told you nothing until you opened it. August producer prices rose 0.4% with core +0.3%, both in line — but the annual rate accelerated to 5.4% (core 4.7%), and the internals are the oil war in one line: goods +1.1%, energy +4.2%, diesel +24.1%, against services +0.1%. That is inflation arriving through the pipeline rather than through demand, which is precisely the kind a rate hike cannot fix — and the Fed meets on it in six days.
headline.summary: The tape is splitting hard along that line. Energy is the only green on the board — COP +2.01%, XOM +1.86%, CVX +1.66%, MPC +1.59% with Brent pressing $102 — while semis are being sold: MU −3.00%, SNDK −2.64%, ASML −2.55%, TSM −1.92% into its own sales update. QQQ −1.22% is breaking Wednesday's inside bar to the downside before the bell. The 10-year sits at 4.84%, its highest since October 2023, with the 30-year at 5.3% — and Bessent's plan to triple buybacks to $6B was read as confirmation of supply stress rather than relief.

overview: Three dated events and one that matters more than the other two. The ECB decides this morning with a 25bp hike to 2.50% fully priced — Lagarde's tone is the event, not the number — and a 30-year auction at 12:00pm CT lands with the long bond already at 5.3%. Then Oracle reports after the close: consensus near $1.75 EPS on roughly $19.1B revenue (+28%), with the whole AI trade watching whether that $638B backlog converts, and options pricing a double-digit move. Wednesday's session was the third straight down day — Dow −406 to 52,381, S&P −0.5%, Russell worst at −1.3% — and the pattern underneath has been consistent all week: the index drifts, breadth rots, energy takes the only bid. One thing did change on the flow board. After four straight sessions of ask-leaning index prints, Wednesday's largest print on the whole tape was IVV $1.1B on the bid, and cumulative flow went with it — AVGO $1.9B bid, NVDA $1.8B bid, GOOGL $1.4B bid, all bid-side on a red day. One session does not unwind four, but it is the first crack in that pattern since the inflation week began.

setups: Wednesday was a 2 Up — it took Tuesday's 163.11 high to 165.18 and closed 164.23 above it. Premarket 167.28 clears that high as well. This is no longer only a geopolitical trade: this morning's PPI put energy +4.2% and diesel +24.1% into the producer data, which is the oil war showing up in the official inflation file. The complex is confirming across the board — COP +2.01%, CVX +1.66%, MPC +1.59% with MPC at an all-time high — and CVX and COP were the only bullish kickers on the entire board Wednesday. Over 165.18 continues it. The Oman “safe route” headline is still the single print that ends this.

Wednesday sat entirely inside Tuesday — H 719.70 / L 714.02 inside 721.886 / 715.57 — and closed 716.31 mid-range with no trigger. Premarket 707.56 is six and a half points below the inside bar's low, which resolves it decisively down before the bell. The driver is underneath: MU −3.00%, SNDK −2.64%, ASML −2.55%, TSM −1.92% into its own monthly sales update, and ADI −2.18% despite a $91.3M mid-side print at the open. Under 714.02 the inside bar is resolved. The caution: an inside bar that gaps well beyond its own range often sees a retest of the level, and 714.02 is the line to watch on any bounce.

Wednesday broke both of Tuesday's regular-session extremes — H 165.15 over 164.87, L 160.36 under 161.18 — and closed 161.63, an outside bar closing in its lower half. Premarket 159.10 is below that low. It reports after the close against consensus of roughly $1.75 EPS on $19.1B revenue (+28%), with options pricing a double-digit move. Two things sit on opposite sides: the stock already failed to hold a 5.5% gap earlier this week two sessions before the print, and Wednesday's board carried a $371M bid print in ORCL after hours — institutional size positioning into the number. No level survives a double-digit implied move; this is an event, not a setup.

darkpool.note: The streak broke. After four consecutive sessions of ask-leaning index prints, Wednesday's largest print on the whole tape was IVV $1.1B on the bid — the first bid lean up top since the run began. Cumulative flow went the same way: AVGO $1.9B (bid), NVDA $1.8B (bid) and GOOGL $1.4B (bid) topped the board, all bid-side on a day the Dow fell 406. NVDA was the top ex-ETF print for a third straight session at $750M, but the side has walked bid → ask → mixed across those three days, which is a migration worth watching rather than a signal. The one to sit with is ORCL $371M (bid, AH) — nine-figure size parked in Oracle the night before earnings, with a $232M CRM bid further down the same list. On the ETF side, IEFA drew $658M, international developed-markets money showing up in size the night before an ECB decision. One bid session does not unwind four ask ones, but it is the first crack in that pattern since the inflation week began.

tts.text: Thursday September tenth, premarket. P P I came in on consensus and told you nothing until you opened it. August producer prices rose zero point four percent with core up zero point three, both in line, but the annual rate accelerated to five point four percent, with core at four point seven. And the internals are the oil war in one line. Goods up one point one percent, energy up four point two, diesel up twenty four point one, against services up just zero point one. That is inflation arriving through the pipeline rather than through demand, which is precisely the kind a rate hike cannot fix, and the Fed meets on it in six days. The tape is splitting hard along that line. Energy is the only green on the board, with Conoco up two point zero one percent, Exxon up one point eight six, Chevron up one point six six and Marathon up one point five nine, while Brent presses one hundred two dollars. Semis are being sold. Micron down three percent, SanDisk down two point six four, A S M L down two point five five and Taiwan Semi down one point nine two into its own sales update. Q Q Q down one point two two percent is breaking Wednesday's inside bar to the downside before the bell.

It reports after the close with options pricing a double digit move. No level survives that.

tts.label: Levels
tts.text: The levels that matter today. Exxon, one sixty five eighteen, Wednesday's high, already cleared premarket. Q Q Q, seven fourteen oh two, Wednesday's inside bar low, and premarket is six points under it. Oracle, one sixty three sixty on the downside, but understand that a double digit implied move makes every level decorative tonight. Apple, three seventeen eighty six, and it is fifty six cents away after completing a failed two down on Wednesday. Five straight sessions have failed at that number. A sixth makes it a ceiling rather than a level. Micron, nine ninety two twenty nine, Wednesday's low, is the reference beneath a three percent premarket decline. And Taiwan Semi has its monthly sales update today while trading down one point nine two percent into it. Three dated events. The E C B this morning with twenty five basis points to two point five zero fully priced, so Lagarde's tone is the event rather than the number. A thirty year auction at noon central with the long bond already at five point three. And Oracle after the close with a six hundred thirty eight billion dollar backlog to defend.
